transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM); Anita Patel (Sapphire CISO), Michael Lee (Head of IT), Santiago Ruiz (Security Engineer), Laura Chen (Compliance)

Summary: brief SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review. Customer requested reports, trust center access, controls mapping, and clarification on RBAC/SSO, audit logs retention, and KMS options for Dedicated/Private deployments. Action items and follow ups agreed.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Anita, Michael, thanks for making time, we'll keep this focused on your SOC2 / ISO posture questions and the controls mapping, Priya will cover technical details.
00:12 Anita: thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We're mostly looking for evidence and ability to map your controls to our control framework, and then some specifics around key management and data residency.
00:22 Priya: great, yeah so we'll run through what we can share - SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, trust center for continuous docs, and then go into RBAC, SSO, audit logs, encryption and private options. Quick note: some names in our portal are slightly different, you'll see 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes show as 'Dedicated cluster' in our docs.
00:40 Michael: okeh - and what's your retention on audit logs by default, like 90 days? our internal req is 1 year for audit trails.
00:50 Priya: default hosted logs are 90 days in the console UI, but we offer extended retention as an add-on - and for Dedicated/Private deployments you can export logs to your SIEM (SPLUNK/Datadog) or to your S3 with a retention policy you control. For Private on-prem you manage retention entirely.
01:05 Anita: ok that's promising. For KMS we need to understand whether you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys for production.
01:15 Priya: yes we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP KMS for hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments you can integrate with your on-prem HSM; we have HSM integration guides. There is a difference though - in hosted we use envelope encryption where Redwood controls the outer key unless you enable BYOK. If you enable BYOK, keys are in your KMS and we never persist plaintext keys.
01:36 Santiago: just to clarify, does BYOK mean you never have access to the plaintext model weights or any decryption keys?
01:42 Priya: correct - BYOK keeps the master key in your control. Redwood's runtime uses ephemeral data keys for encryption in memory, and they are not stored long-term; auditor notes are in the KMS section of the SOC2 report.
01:56 Jordan: I'll make sure the SOC2 report has the relevant KMS notes called out, and we'll include the auditor statement.
02:02 Laura: what about RBAC and SSO? we need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO with our IdP.
02:08 Priya: we support SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning for user groups, and granular RBAC (roles: admin, developer, viewer, auditor). We also have session timeout and MFA enforcement options which you can set via policy.
02:23 Michael: does the RBAC include token-level restrictions? like restricting model access per team or route-level policies?
02:30 Priya: yes, route and model-level access control exists for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we provide per-api-key scoping and project-level access - you can scope keys to only embeddings or only generation. For enterprise customers we can add more granular route policies.
02:46 Anita: audit logs - can you provide the actual audit log schema? we need to map fields to our SIEM.
02:51 Priya: yes we'll share the audit event schema. It includes timestamp, user_id, api_key_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_ip, response_code, and token_count. Some fields may vary slightly between hosted and Dedicated. We'll include schema in the controls mapping doc.
03:10 Santiago: any PII/ePHI handling notes? we're healthcare, so HIPAA concerns, data residency within us-east for PHI, and we need BAAs.
03:21 Jordan: Redwood can sign a BAA for Private deployments; for Hosted we have a few customers using hosted with BAA under specific contractual terms - I need to check product constraints but we'll confirm. We'll put that as an action item.
03:36 Priya: technical note: for customers with strict PHI limits we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so you can isolate workloads and control network boundaries and KMS. For hosted we do support data processing agreements but some controls are limited.
03:50 Michael: are pen test reports available? we usually need recent external pentest summaries.
03:54 Jordan: yes, we have pentest summaries and remediation statements. Some details are in Trust Center; full reports can be provided under NDA.
04:05 Anita: trust center - how do we get access? read-only? do you provide an auditor account?
04:11 Priya: we can provision a temporary "trust-center-viewer" account for your compliance team. For external auditors we can create auditor accounts or provide a signed bundle (reports + evidence) depending on the auditor's needs. We'll send a link and temporary creds.
04:25 Laura: controls mapping - we need a spreadsheet mapping your controls to ISO 27001 annex A and our internal control IDs. can you map to SOC 2 CC and ISO controls?
04:34 Carlos: yes, we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A controls to our internal policies and evidence sources. We'll tailor a version for Sapphire Health and highlight evidence items you can pull from Trust Center.
04:46 Santiago: any notes on model weights / data retention for embeddings? do you keep customer prompts? we need to know deletion semantics and retention windows and how to confirm deletion for audit.
05:02 Priya: by default we do not use customer prompts to train models; we can sign that in the DPA. For hosted, ephemeral cache may persist for performance but we have options to disable caching. We keep metadata logs; for deletion you can request data deletion and we'll provide a confirmation. For Dedicated/Private, you fully control storage.
05:25 Michael: network controls - VPC peering, PrivateLink, ingress/egress restrictions?
05:31 Priya: for Dedicated we offer VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink; for Private deployments you can use your network controls and private subnets. We also support IP allowlists and firewall rules at the route level.
05:46 Anita: ok this is helpful. can we get an explicit statement in writing about separation of duties for ops vs engineering? auditors ask that.
05:55 Jordan: yes, we'll include an SoD statement and role definitions in the evidence bundle.
06:00 Laura: SLA and incident reporting - do you have a security incident playbook and notification window for breaches?
06:06 Carlos: we have an incident response plan and SLA tiers. For security incidents that affect customer data we notify customers within our contractual window (we'll provide the exact window in the package). We also publish uptime SLAs for Dedicated customers.
06:18 Santiago: one more small item - can we run a short benchmark to validate latency and confirm the KV cache behavior on Dedicated? we'll need an SE-led session to validate perf with our traffic patterns.
06:30 Priya: absolutely, we'll set up a POC cluster or a dedicated perf run - we'll need details on your expected qps, average prompt lengths, and token distribution. Priya: (laugh) I mean we'll need those metrics, not me.
06:40 Michael: QPS around 50 sustained with spikes to 200, typical prompt ~120 tokens, sometimes longer.
06:48 Priya: great, we'll scope perf test and include suggested quantization/batching config.
06:55 Jordan: recap - Action items: Jordan to share SOC2/ISO reports; Priya to create trust center viewer and share audit schema; Carlos to provide controls mapping spreadsheet; Santiago to send audit queries/retention specifics; schedule perf deep dive week of 12/22. Any objections?
07:12 Anita: none, thanks, that covers it.
07:16 Jordan: perfect. We'll follow up via email with links and docs, and I'll attach the SOC reports. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
